ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 7:3 ratio of high-intensity white pixels to low-intensity black pixels across the visible ventral surface area.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Centrally localized high-intensity (white) contiguous regions covering approximately 70% of the surface. Low-intensity (black) pixels define the perimeter, with significant thickness at the lateral tips. High-frequency black mottling is concentrated at the basal insertion point and transitions into the high-intensity regions through stippled clusters.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: U-shaped central depression with a vertex angle of approximately 45 degrees; vertical depth occupies roughly 15% of the total vertical height of the fluke lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Highly irregular serration profile along the trailing edge boundary; peaks and valleys exhibit higher amplitude (approx. 8-12 pixels) on the distal thirds of the lobes, transitioning to smoother, lower-frequency variations near the median notch.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave sweep from the median notch to the lateral tips; outer edges exhibit a sharp posterior-lateral curvature.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Multiple discrete, circular low-intensity pixel clusters (<10 pixel diameter) scattered within the white central masks, primarily localized in the lower medial quadrants.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Detection of several thin, unaligned dark linear pixel disruptions crossing the white field on the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A series of 4-5 parallel, vertically-oriented low-intensity linear marks (rake marks) visible on the right lobe white surface area; irregular jagged indentation on the distal trailing edge of the left lobe suggesting minor tissue loss.
other_distinctive_markers: Distinctive hook-shaped black pigmentation extensions protruding from the lower boundary into the white field of the left lobe.
